sourceState: Scheduling Wave A: the bounded RRULE expansion engine and derived due-queue query ported verbatim (19 + 6 pinned cases green under their pinned names), plus the writer-lane-authored source-agnostic due-occurrence seam (IDueOccurrenceSource / RruleDueOccurrenceSource / CompositeDueOccurrenceSource, 3 seam tests) required by the user ruling of 2026-08-16 so the ticket-086 relative-chain generator lands behind the same port later. The pinned DI extension is retained without an explicit M.E.DI.Abstractions reference (implicit on net11-preview). ADR-0117/0123 moves the due seam and queue to hlp.blocks.scheduling, leaving the RRULE producer and shared NodaTime wall-clock resolver here. T-491/module-admission moves the unchanged shared availability contract and its type closure here; Calendar keeps the interpreter and supply model. T-1197/bounded-expansion (interface revision 9) uses one 50000-unit due-query budget across rule input, supplied overrides, recurrence periods and matched dates, with a 3660-date requested-window maximum. List-returning producer methods retain their unbudgeted Calendar/Booking contract and separate 1000-result cap. Bound metadata is null only when input text exhausts work before classification. Extreme zoned UNTIL dates are handled without overflowing local DateTime. Control rulings 1371/1372/1378; T-1202 owns bounding calendar composers.
nextGate: Wave B ports the calendar domain engine (packages/blocks-calendar, 163 cases); Wave C re-proves the 88 host rows at narrowed seams and flips the scheduling gate only through the scheduling-capability-vertical.
